Granted, this is a jail and not a prison but I can tell you from spending nearly a decade working in a prison that, as long as you're keeping yourself hydrated, you'll be fine. It's uncomfortable as hell but you'll be fine. We spent time inside those dorms with our inmates and in those cellblocks. You really didn't want to be on the upper tiers during the summer. During the Winter, fine but sure as shit not during the summer.

Most of our inmates had some creative means of keeping cool. Taking a bandanna, soaking it in cool water and then draping it over the back of their neck was one, regularly drinking water was another. The dorms were also equipped with coolers full of nothing but ice and there were ice calls a few times per day and one per night.

The hottest period in my history there was during one of the hurricanes where power was knocked out and the generators were a little on the dicey side.

Here's the kicker, there were massive fans in the corners of the dorms, mounted to the ceilings and when they were on, shit got loud. They helped but not by much. I learned toward the end of my career that the inmates had been given a choice, Cable TV or AC, they chose Cable TV.

For most in Jail, like the article says, they haven't been convicted of anything but I can guarantee you, upon release, that's something to remember. If you find yourself in that situation, just stay hydrated. Whatever you do, drink water, do what you can to keep cool and don't go popping off about it. This article isn't doing anything other than really screaming "LOOK AT HOW INHUMANE THIS IS!!!" but the thing it, this jail has probably always been like this. It's uncomfortable as hell, yes but the officers are enduring that just as much as the inmates there.
